'''Cxc''' is a programming language for the Apple ecosystem that targets the libobjc runtime shared with Objective-C and Swift, so programs interoperate directly with Foundation, AppKit, and UIKit without a bridge layer.

cxc is object-oriented and functional with no imperative control, which means no assignments, no loops, no breaks, no continues. Logic lives in pure functions, and state transitions and iteration both happen through message passing. A program is a graph of ''atoms'', each owning state and running a lifecycle state machine. Message-triggered transitions replace imperative control flow, and no state is shared across atom boundaries.

== Multimodal introspection ==

I built cxc so every running program stays inspectable through more than one surface. Every compiled program can emit a lifecycle trace (<code>CXC_TRACE_PATH=./trace.jsonl ./program</code>). The browser viewer (<code>cxc view trace.jsonl</code>) renders it as a zoomable graph of atom messaging, fan-out, and per-arm dispatch. Hot-reload swaps methods on live programs without restart, and a REPL socket delivers messages and fault-injection into running programs.
